data.narrative:
Xanadu Quantum Technologies is a public-stage quantum computing company that has raised $245M to date. The valuation analysis relies on a peer-median approach across five same-sector, same-stage comparables: IonQ ($13.0B), D-Wave Quantum ($6.3B), Rigetti Computing ($4.5B), Infleqtion ($1.9B), and Archer Materials ($60M). This peer set spans a wide valuation range from $60M to $13.0B, reflecting heterogeneous commercial maturity and technology differentiation within the quantum computing sector.

The peer-median method yields an implied valuation of $4.5B for Xanadu, representing the midpoint of publicly-traded quantum computing companies. Given the limited methodological input (one triangulation method applied), the analysis supports a range of $3.8B to $5.2B, centered at $4.5B. This range reflects ±15% variance around the median estimate. The quantum computing peer universe remains volatile and thinly traded; valuations are not yet anchored by profitability or standardized revenue multiples.

Key uncertainties include the absence of revenue-based or discounted cash flow validation, the extreme spread within the comparable set (220x from floor to ceiling), and limited private market pricing data. The single-method triangulation provides narrow statistical support. Investors should treat this median estimate as a reference point rather than a precise valuation, pending evidence of differentiated technical performance or commercial traction relative to the peer set.
